extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern’s LifeSecure is a disability insurance product that pays a regular monthly benefit for total and permanent disability or for inability to perform at least 2 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). The monthly payout is stated as “up to S$5,000” for up to a lifetime, and it is intended to help cover disability-related care at home or in hospital and related aids/equipment and home modifications. For stand-alone LifeSecure, a lump sum death benefit equal to 3 times the monthly benefit applies if the life insured dies during the coverage term. A separate “payback benefit” is payable after a deferment period (90 days or 180 days), and then pays a lump sum of 3 times or 6 times the monthly benefit insured. The brochure also describes an out-of-school disability benefit for a child aged 7–16, adding S$500 per month on top of the insured child monthly benefit (ending at age 16, with at least 12 monthly installments).
quality_notes: Document gives the core benefit mechanics, but does not clearly state the full set of plan options (e.g., how the monthly benefit is selected beyond examples).

Premium tables are provided for illustrative S$1,000 monthly benefit (stand-alone) and S$500 monthly benefit (as a rider), but eligibility/age limits for the adult coverage are not explicitly enumerated beyond footnotes.

policies.quick_summary: Disability insurance that pays monthly benefits for total and permanent disability or inability to perform at least 2 ADLs, with optional payback and (for stand-alone) a death lump sum. Also includes an out-of-school disability benefit for children aged 7–16 (adding S$500/month on top of the insured child benefit). Can be purchased stand-alone or as a rider attached to selected whole life plans offered by Great Eastern (as stated). Monthly benefit shown as up to S$5,000 for up to a lifetime; payback lump sum after a deferment period (3x or 6x the monthly benefit). No cash value/investment feature stated.
coverage_scope: Inability to perform at least 2 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)
Out-of-school disability benefit for a child aged 7–16 (where applicable)
Lump sum payback after deferment period (3x or 6x monthly benefit)
Stand-alone death benefit of 3 times the monthly benefit during coverage term
policies.residency_requirements: Product “applies mainly to Singapore Citizen/PR” and requires “certain residency requirements before you can apply for a policy or renew it.”
policies.eligibility_notes: Child out-of-school disability benefit applies to “your child, age between 7 and 16 years old”. Other adult eligibility/underwriting is not specified in the brochure.
policies.coverage_term_description: Premium tables and narrative reference coverage term options such as “up to age 65”, “up to age 80”, and “lifetime” (illustrated). Exact selection rules are not stated.
policies.premium_payment_term_description: Premium tables illustrate “Premium payment term” options “up to age 65” or “up to age 80” depending on coverage term, but the brochure does not provide a full ruleset.
policy_termination_events: Policy ends or is terminated prematurely (no cash value stated)
important_caveats: If purchased as a stand-alone plan, a lump sum death benefit of 3 times the monthly benefit is payable if death occurs during the coverage term (rider purchase is described separately but death benefit mechanics are only stated in the stand-alone context).

Payback benefit is payable following a deferment period of 90 days or 180 days starting from when the life assured starts suffering the ADL inability or total and permanent disability, during which “no benefit is payable”.
No savings/investment feature is stated; brochure states there is no cash value if the policy ends or if terminated prematurely.
Out-of-school disability benefit ends when the life assured attains age 16, and is subject to a minimum of 12 monthly installments having been paid.
